narrative: Fire and drought responses lead today's brief. Three studies examine post-fire forests: one tests whether subsurface nitrogen fuels recovery in northern conifer stands, one links pyrodiversity to phylogenetic and taxonomic patterns in post-fire plant communities, and one shows rising fire severity changes how plant taxonomic and functional diversity assemble. On the climate side, biological crust cover increased the sensitivity of ephemeral plant productivity to extreme drought, and a Nature Climate Change paper reports that warming boosts the frequency and intensity of southern African rainfall extremes. Belowground partnerships feature in Functional Ecology and New Phytologist, where arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal systems differ in carbon storage responses to nitrogen and in phosphorus foraging, and root hairs and mycorrhiza emerge as alternative conserved strategies. At landscape scale, newly planted woodlands improved connectivity for fauna, flora and fungi, while rewilding of large animals coincided with declines of small ones in post-agrarian landscapes. Methods news includes the updated camtrapR package and a Vendi information gain approach to active learning for camera trap images.
